Use this template when proposing research work, submitting reproducible artifacts, or requesting methodological feedback. Do not include any personally identifying information (PII) or private data in the issue; note how sensitive materials will be handled instead.

**Title**

A concise title for the research proposal or artifact.

**Summary / abstract**

A short summary of the research question or artifact and its intended contribution.

**Background and motivation**

Why this research is important; link to relevant literature or repository materials.

**Objectives and research questions**

List the primary objectives and specific research questions or hypotheses.

**Methodology**

Describe study design, data sources (public or private), data collection methods, and analysis approach. If private or sensitive data are required, describe how access will be managed and confirm that nothing sensitive will be committed to this repository.

**Reproducibility checklist**

- [ ] Description of data provenance and licensing
- [ ] Minimal scripts or notebooks to reproduce core results (or a plan for them)
- [ ] Environment and dependency notes (language, package versions)
- [ ] Clear README describing how to run analyses

**Ethics and approvals**

If human subjects are involved, state whether IRB/ethics approval is required and provide details or an approval reference (do not attach sensitive documents).

**Expected outputs**

Describe expected outputs (e.g., figures, tables, protocols, templates) and where they would be placed in the repository.

**Timeline and collaborators**

Estimated timeline and people involved.

**Additional notes**

Any other considerations, limitations, or requests for maintainers (e.g., data hosting, compute resources).
